text:
maya: FYI I opened a docs PR to replace the big cost/latency heatmap with a compact CSV example and updated tracing-hook usage. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4130

own: Thanks. Which snippets need updates? I can run markdown lint and sandbox.

maya: Two snippets: console/examples/heatmap.md (node + py). Need `trace_key` rename, and a short note about batching tradeoffs.

tara: I can do node. jen, want python?

jen: I'll take python and run the sandbox. Also prefer showing p95 + avg for latency SLOs.

own: Linter found code-fence language missing and a broken anchor in the cost table. I'll open a tiny patch and drop it into your branch.

maya: Please add a one-line "how to read" clarifying prefetch lowers tail latency but increases unit cost. Use relative deltas, not absolute numbers.

jen: Draft python snippet: `from redwood import ConsoleClient\nclient = ConsoleClient()\nresp = client.trace_hook(model="xgen-7b", trace_key="session_123", prefetch="windowed")\nprint(f"p95: {resp.metrics['p95_latency_ms']} ms, cost: ${resp.metrics['cost_per_token_usd']}")`

own: Looks good. Replace `session_123` with example placeholder and use labels. I'll merge my linter patch into your PR after CI.

tara: Updated node snippet and removed old `traceid` refs. Left an inline note to reviewers about SDK rename.

docs-bot: CI queued for PR 4130 and linter PR 4131 8a00.

maya: Action items: owen - land anchor fix, jen - push python snippet and sandbox results, tara - confirm node delta numbers, maya - replace absolute table with relative CSV. Waiting on CI green to merge. :thumbsup:
